items.title: Make the death screen name the thing that actually killed you
items.why: handlePlayerDeath reads gs._lastDamageBy, which no module has written since the S163 enemy-frame extraction, then falls back to the nearest enemy's `.type` — a field enemies never carry (they carry `typeIndex`). killerType is therefore always undefined: recordDeathByEnemy never fires, MOST WANTED killed-by counts stay at zero, adaptive telegraphing keys on gs._telegraphMult[e.type] (undefined), the Run Coach 'what killed you' pattern never forms, ghost/run-history killedByType is always null, and the boss-nemesis branch would throw on an out-of-scope `best` if it were ever reached. BOT ROYALE flood damage bypasses applyObservedPlayerDamage entirely, so a drowning is invisible to the observed final-damage receipt.
items.recipe: Add a pure resolveDeathAttribution(gs) in src/systems/deathAttribution.js that prefers the last damage-sequence event (sourceType/sourceName/kind), falls back to the nearest live enemy by typeIndex, and reports the evidence level. Route handlePlayerDeath, ghost persistence, and run-history killedBy through it; key adaptive telegraphing by typeIndex; record royale flood damage as an observed hazard named 'Sewer flood'; cover every path with unit tests.
executionLog: L2 shipped: src/systems/deathAttribution.js resolves the observed damage-sequence event first and the nearest live enemy (typeIndex) as a labelled hypothesis; handlePlayerDeath, ghost persistence, run history (bounded deathAttribution receipt), adaptive telegraphing (typeIndex), and nemesis tracking route through it; royale flood damage is an observed hazard 'Sewer flood'. Courts: deathAttribution 4/4, runSession, modeDefinition, deathFlow green; strict lint 0.

items.title: Show what the run was worth in the mode you were playing
items.why: The death and victory screens carry only a mode label (plus a royale placement). A SEWER EXTRACTION death never says how much loot went down the drain or how close the evac was; a HOLD THE THRONE death never says how many thrones were held; a BOSS GAUNTLET death never says which boss stopped the run or whether par was beaten. The mode-specific stake — the thing Soul pillar 2 says a defeat must convert into a lesson — is dropped at the exact moment it matters.
items.recipe: Give each mode definition a pure outcome(gs) that returns a bounded {headline, detail, stat} receipt (extraction: loot lost or banked, crates, alarm state; royale: placement, flushed, phase; throne: captured/lost; gauntlet: bosses down and par delta). Build it in deathFlow.buildModeOutcomeReceipt, pass it through buildDeathScreenProps, and render it under the title with data-testid so tests and pixels can bind to it.
executionLog: L2 shipped: every mode definition exposes a pure outcome(gs); getModeOutcomeReceipt bounds it to mode-outcome-v1; buildDeathScreenProps carries it and DeathScreen renders data-testid="mode-outcome" under the title. Courts: modeDefinition outcome 4/4, deathFlow passthrough + source contract green; strict lint 0.

items.title: Keep announcements on the screen when the world scrolls
items.why: Floating texts are drawn in arena coordinates under the camera translate (S165). Twenty-eight App.jsx call sites write level-ups, DOCTRINE READY, objective ACTIVE, MISSION COMPLETE, synergy, and perk roasts at GW()/2, GH()/2 — the centre of the top-left viewport-sized window of the arena — and BOT ROYALE writes its DROP IN and THE SEWER FLOODS phase calls at the arena centre. In the two scrolled modes those announcements are off-screen whenever the camera has moved, which is most of the time.
items.recipe: Add addScreenText to transientPresentation (a floating text flagged screen:true), render screen-flagged texts outside the camera translate in drawGame, migrate every viewport-centre App.jsx call site, and hand modes an announce(gs, text, color) helper through the mode context so mode callouts never need arena coordinates. Guard with a unit test and a source contract that forbids world-anchored centre announcements.
executionLog: L2 shipped: addScreenText/announce in transientPresentation, drawGame paints screen-flagged texts outside the camera translate, 57 App.jsx call sites migrated (GW()/2 and VX/VY announcement sites), mode ctx carries announce/viewW/viewH and the four mode definitions use it. Courts: transientPresentation, modeDefinition, arena-spawn-wiring source contract green; strict lint 0.

items.title: Give wave-start mode hooks the arena, not the viewport
items.why: createModeState and stepMode receive arena dimensions, but onModeWaveStart is called with { W: GW(), H: GH() } — the viewport. SEWER EXTRACTION spawns three crates per wave from that context, so every crate after the first wave lands inside the top-left viewport-sized window of the 1.5x arena; the S166 'distributes loot across the scrolling world' claim holds only for wave 1.
items.recipe: Resolve arena bounds once at the wave-start seam and pass them (plus viewW/viewH for screen-space needs) to onModeWaveStart; add a unit test that drives onWaveStart with arena dimensions and asserts crates land beyond the viewport; extend the arena-spawn wiring source contract.
executionLog: L2 shipped: onModeWaveStart receives resolveArenaBounds(gs, GW(), GH()) plus viewW/viewH; extraction wave crates land across the 1.5x arena. Courts: modeDefinition wave-start distribution 36/36 crates, arena-spawn-wiring contract green.
